extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and researchers interested in Romesh Ranganathan or contemporary British comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography page describing the career, style, background, and achievements of a stand-up comedian and television/radio presenter. Useful for extracting descriptive criteria that signal comedic style and career success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy style
rubrics_metrics.description: His style of comedy is deadpan and often self-deprecating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly identifies 'deadpan' and 'self-deprecating' as defining characteristics of his comedic voice; these stylistic labels operate as criteria for categorising his material and performance approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility and panel-show presence as a career indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Has made numerous appearances on television comedy panel shows and has been a regular panellist on The Apprentice: You're Fired!, Play to the Whistle, and The Museum of Curiosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequent panel-show appearances and regular panellist roles are presented as markers of industry visibility and comedian profile. The page lists many such appearances (e.g., Have I Got News for You, Mock the Week, 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown) which imply importance of TV panel work in evaluating a comedian's prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tours and live-venue scale
rubrics_metrics.description: He completed his first major tour, Irrational Live, in 2016; he performed in large venues such as the Hammersmith Apollo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful touring and performing in large, named venues are treated as evidence of commercial/stand-up success. The biography uses tour names, dates, and venue size (Hammersmith Apollo) as indicators of standing as a live performer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting and presenting original programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: He has presented comedy programmes Judge Romesh and The Ranganation, as well as starring in the travel programme The Misadventures of Romesh Ranganathan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creating or fronting named TV series (comedy, travelogue, panel shows) is presented as a professional milestone; being the presenter/host signals a different, higher-profile role than guesting. The page lists multiple presenter credits across genres as evidence of range and achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020, Ranganathan won the BAFTA TV Award for Best Features for The Misadventures of Romesh Ranganathan. In 2021, he won the BAFTA TV Award for Best Entertainment Performance for The Ranganation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major awards (BAFTA wins and nominations, Royal Television Society awards, Audio and Radio Industry Award) are recorded as formal measures of critical/industry recognition and are used on the page to indicate the quality/impact of his work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi‑medium output and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Credits include film, television, stand-up specials, radio (hosts a weekly radio show 'For The Love of Hip-Hop'), books (autobiography Straight Outta Crawley), theatre, and music guest appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page enumerates work across stand-up, TV, radio, books and film; breadth of mediums and a varied filmography are implicit criteria for evaluating a modern entertainer's career versatility and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal background and identity in material
rubrics_metrics.description: He travelled to Sri Lanka to explore his ancestry (Asian Provocateur) and is described as having Sri Lankan Tamil parents and a Hindu upbringing; his early life details (e.g., father's conviction, upbringing) are noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography links personal history and heritage to projects (e.g., Asian Provocateur) — implying that authenticity, personal storytelling, and engagement with background/identity are evaluative dimensions of his creative output.
